5f:Tfba,## The defect (6th recurrence)

A ~59px strip of `#160d07` (the `--launch-bg` / `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR`) sits below the "Ask Sol" composer down to the true screen bottom on the **installed iOS Safari standalone PWA** (home-indicator iPhone). The wallpaper (`AppBackground` → `ImageBackground`, a `fixed inset-0` cover layer) is not reaching the true physical bottom, so `#root`'s dark bg shows through the gap.

## Why every prior fix failed (proven root cause)

Every prior PR (#14067/#14184/#14224/#14293/#14411/#14539/#14996) pinned the fixed-layer reclaim to:

```css
bottom: calc(-1 * max(0px, 100lvh - 100dvh))
```

This bets that `100lvh` (large viewport) exceeds `100dvh` (dynamic viewport) by the collapse delta. **On this device it doesn't.** The app `body` is `position: fixed`, which collapses the ICB for its `position: fixed` descendants to the LAYOUT (small) viewport. When that ICB has collapsed, the CSS length engine resolves **both** `lvh` and `dvh` against the same collapsed box, so `100lvh - 100dvh === 0` — **every reclaim is a no-op**. The CSS units can't see the true screen height from inside the collapsed fixed-body box.

That's why the strip survived 5 CSS-only fixes AND their tests: the tests only re-asserted the calc **string** was present in the source, never the measured result.

## The fix: measure the real gap in JS

New `packages/ui/src/platform/standalone-bottom-reclaim.ts`:
- Measures `trueHeight (visualViewport.height + offsetTop, or innerHeight) − layoutHeight (documentElement.clientHeight)`
- Writes it to `--standalone-bottom-reclaim` on `:root`
- Re-measures on `visualViewport` resize/scroll + `orientationchange` (rAF-coalesced, idempotent install, disposes on re-install / clear)
- Standalone/native-gated; on web/desktop/Android the measured gap is **0** → true no-op, no listeners attached

All six reclaim sites now use `calc(-1 * var(--standalone-bottom-reclaim, 0px))` (shared `STANDALONE_BOTTOM_RECLAIM_OFFSET` constant): `ImageBackground`, `ShaderBackground`, `ProgrammableShaderBackground`, App `app-safe-area-floor`, and the `ContinuousChatOverlay` composer (rest state only — keyboard-lift path untouched).

Also **removes the cosmetic warm-ember bottom-floor gradient** from `ImageBackground` — it only existed to disguise the strip under the useless CSS-unit reclaim; with the measured reclaim the wallpaper's own pixels reach the true bottom (lock-screen style).

## Tests pin the MEASURED gap (not a string)

`standalone-bottom-reclaim.test.ts` reproduces the collapsed geometry (layout `873` / true `932`) and asserts:
- `measureStandaloneBottomGap()` === `59`
- === `0` on non-collapsed (web/desktop/Android) surfaces — regression guard
- never negative when the keyboard shrinks the visual viewport
- clamped on absurd transient (mid-rotation) deltas
- the applied `--standalone-bottom-reclaim` var === `59px` (would be `0` under the old CSS-unit calc — the exact failing-on-device case)
- idempotent install / no duplicate listeners

Updated `AppBackground.test.tsx` + `standalone-pwa-lockdown.test.ts` to assert the measured var (and the absence of the dead CSS-unit calc as a value + the removed cosmetic floor).

## Correctness notes
- **No regression on web/desktop/Android:** measured gap is exactly 0 → reclaim is `calc(-1 * 0px)` === 0.
- **Bottom taps reach chat:** every reclaimed layer (`app-safe-area-floor`, wallpapers) is `pointer-events-none` at `z-[-1]`; the strip was `#root` bg paint, never a pointer capture.
- **Did NOT touch** index.html / vite.config.ts / turbo.json / bun.lock. No new raw hex, no new backdrop-blur.

Part of #14783 and #14747.62:Tb27,## What

Long-press the bare home wallpaper (~500ms) to open a background quick-picker. The gesture is a new **entry point** into the existing background system, not a second system: the sheet embeds the shared \`BackgroundSettingsControls\`, so every choice writes through the same \`useBackgroundConfig\` / \`ui-preferences\` store that Settings and the Background view use. Selections apply live (optimistic) and persist through the identical path.

## UX flow ("intuitive af")

- **Long-press** the empty wallpaper. While a candidate press is held, the home content dims and settles back a hair (transform/opacity only, stilled under \`prefers-reduced-motion\`) so the wallpaper reads as the thing being acted on.
- At ~500ms a **medium haptic** fires and a **bottom sheet** rises (matching the app's sheet idiom) with a tinted scrim behind it.
- The sheet shows the live catalog thumbnails (curated + your uploads/generations), the current one marked, tap to apply **instantly**.
- Dismiss by tapping the scrim, the grabber, the close button, or pressing **Escape**.

## Accidental-trigger protection

- A press on a tile, widget, or any control is ignored (\`canBegin\` guard) so those keep their own tap/long-press semantics; only the bare wallpaper opens the picker.
- Any finger travel past 10px (a vertical scroll of the widget list, or the home to launcher rail swipe) cancels the pending hold, and so does any pointer up/cancel.
- The recognizer is inert while the picker is already open.

## New pieces

- \`useHomeLongPress\` (\`packages/ui/src/gestures/\`): pointer long-press recognizer with a live \`pressing\` affordance flag, per-axis move-cancel slop, and \`canBegin\`/\`enabled\` gating. Sibling of the existing \`usePointerPressAndHold\`.
- \`HomeBackgroundQuickPicker\` (\`packages/ui/src/components/shell/\`): portalled bottom sheet at the shell-overlay z-layer that hosts the shared background controls.
- Wired into \`HomeScreen\` background surface (not widgets/tiles).

## Design compliance

- Design tokens only (no hex added), lucide-react icons only, 44px+ tap targets (close + grabber), no new backdrop-blur (plain tinted scrim), no em-dashes in copy.

- \`useHomeLongPress\` unit tests: timer commit, \`pressing\` flag lifecycle, move-cancel / scroll-cancel / up / cancel, \`canBegin\` + \`enabled\` gating, unmount cleanup.

— [sol-orch]63:T22ea,Fixes #14716, fixes #14717.

Two hardcoded natural-language classifiers were making judgment calls that belong to the model. Both are replaced by structural signals + the LLM seam; net **−181 production lines** in the reminder classifier and **−131** in the triage engine (+474 lines of regression tests).

## #14716 — core triage engine scored urgency/spam by keyword tables

**Root cause.** `packages/core/src/features/messaging/triage/triage-engine.ts` derived `TriageScore.priority` / `suggestedAction` from `URGENCY_KEYWORDS` / `SPAM_KEYWORDS` word-presence: English-only, negation-blind ("no deadline on this" read as urgent; "help" boosted anything), and any mail containing "newsletter"/"unsubscribe" from a non-close contact was auto-labeled spam→skip. The fabricated labels were then surfaced to the model as pre-baked verdicts.

**Fix.** The engine now attaches only typed structural facts the model cannot cheaply derive from text — relationship-derived `contactWeight` (via RelationshipsService), `userRepliedInThread`, `scoredAt` — and `rankScored` orders by recency with contact weight as tie-break. The `MESSAGE` actions (`triageMessages`, `listInbox`, `searchMessages`) surface raw snippets plus these signals (`receivedAtMs`, `isRead`, `contactWeight`, `userRepliedInThread`) and no `priority`/`suggestedAction` fields, so the model reading the ActionResult decides urgency and next action. `TriagePriority`/`SuggestedAction` types are deleted from `@elizaos/core`. `brief.ts` (personal assistant) no longer maps keyword-derived priority into briefing urgency — the compose model judges from the snippet.

**Deleted:** `URGENCY_KEYWORDS`, `SPAM_KEYWORDS`, `findUrgencyKeywords`, `looksLikeSpam`, `scoreToPriority`, `priorityToAction`, priority bump/floor ladder, recency floors, `PRIORITY_RANK` sort, `messageUrgency` (brief.ts).
**Kept:** contact-weight resolution (structural), store/adapter plumbing, action registration.

## #14717 — reminder owner replies classified by regex tables

**Root cause.** `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/lifeops/service-helpers-reminder.ts` resolved reminder state from four substring-matching regex tables + title-token-overlap binding, and consulted the existing LLM classifier (`classifyReminderOwnerResponseSemantically`, which already builds a full prompt with title/adjacency/binding context) **only when the regexes matched nothing**. So `\bskip\b` matched "no, don't skip it" → skipped; `\bdone\b` + title overlap matched "the dentist appointment isn't done yet, ping me tomorrow" → completed — silent wrong state transitions, English-only.

**Fix.** Composition inverted: the semantic (LLM) classifier is primary. The only deterministic path left is an exact-match fast-path (`classifyExactReminderReply`) that fires when the **entire** normalized reply is a bare resolution word or bare duration — exactly the strings the in-app reminder chat choices submit (`done` / `10 minutes` / `skip`, see `appendReminderChatChoices`) — gated on prompt adjacency + `allowStandaloneResolution`. Keyless lanes keep working through it. Without a usable model verdict the reply stays `unrelated` (reason `no_semantic_verdict`) — degraded detection is honest; a keyword guess that flips reminder state is not. A throwing injected classifier now propagates instead of being silently swallowed (the production classifier already returns `null` on model/parse failure).

**Deleted:** `SNOOZE/SKIP/COMPLETE/ACKNOWLEDGE_RESPONSE_PATTERNS`, `matchesAnyPattern`, `tokenizeReminderText` + `TITLE_STOP_WORDS` + `responseReferencesReminder` (title-token binding heuristic), `isStandaloneResolutionResponse`, `isResponseBoundToReminder`, `parseReminderSnoozeRequestFromText` (text sniffer), the fabricated confidence constants (0.86/0.82/0.74/0.35…), the swallowing `catch` in the composer, and the now-producerless `semantic_error` classifier source.
**Kept:** prompt-adjacency window, duration→preset normalization (feeds the fast-path), the semantic prompt/parse layer (unchanged), `decideReminderReviewTransition` and all downstream acknowledgement wiring (untouched per the parallel checkin lane).

65:T12ad,## What & why

The documented web/cloud STT default is `eliza-cloud`, but `resolveBackendKind` in `voice-capture-factory.ts` resolved `eliza-cloud`/`openai` to the browser **Web Speech API** — interactive web capture never sent audio to the cloud STT route. Web STT was therefore engine-dependent (Chrome ships audio to Google's recognizer; some browsers have **no** Web Speech at all), unmeasured, and inconsistent with the provider setting users see.

This wires `eliza-cloud` ASR for real, mirroring the existing local-inference leg:

- **New agent proxy `POST /api/asr/cloud`** (`plugin-elizacloud` -> `handleCloudSttRoute`): forwards a captured WAV as multipart `audio` to `<cloud-base>/voice/stt` — the same upstream the server-side transcription model uses (`transcription.ts` `postApiV1VoiceSttRaw`). Mirrors `/api/tts/cloud` exactly: same base-URL / api-key resolution, same www/apex candidate fan-out, and the **fail-loud** contract (401 when no cloud key, 502 when the upstream is unreachable).
- **New shared `resolveCloudSttCandidateUrls`** (next to `resolveCloudTtsCandidateUrls`).
- **New client `transcribeCloudWav`** POSTs the recorded WAV to the proxy and returns the transcript (throws on non-2xx / empty).
- **`resolveBackendKind`** now routes `eliza-cloud`/`openai` to a new `cloud` backend: it records the same WAV as the local path (`startLocalAsrRecorder`), POSTs it to `/api/asr/cloud`, and emits the cloud transcript as the final segment. Browser SpeechRecognition remains **only** where WAV capture is genuinely unsupported (no `getUserMedia`/`AudioContext`).
- Cloud STT failure surfaces a distinguishable **error** state — no silent downgrade to a browser-final transcript (fail-fast doctrine).
- Docs aligned to reality: `voice-provider-defaults.ts` layering caveat + `STT_SELECTION.md` decision table.

Closes #14372

67:T1f20,## What

Authors a `lane: "live-only"` scenario pack for the **first-run onboarding journey** — the funnel's first mile — covering both entry paths, each ending in the owner's **first reminder actually materializing**:

| Scenario | Path | Domain outcome asserted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `first-run-fast-start-seeds-first-reminder` | fast-start (defaults) | one wake-time answer → default pack seeded; **gm cron anchored to the answered wake time**, gn at 22:00, morning brief on the `wake.confirmed` anchor, check-in `kind` |
| `first-run-customize-walk-seeds-first-reminder` | customize (5 questions) | full walk incl. the **conditional relationships question** (fires only because `follow-ups` is selected) → default pack seeded, anchored to the answered morning window, preferred name persisted |
| `first-run-abandon-resume-no-data-loss` | resume | answer Q1+Q2, abandon, resume on a fresh service instance → **advances to the first unanswered question, no re-asking** → first reminder seeded, anchored to the pre-abandon answer |
| `first-run-channel-fallback-to-in-app` | channel fallback | an unconnected channel → recorded with `fallbackToInApp: true`, warning surfaced, `(fallback)` completion message, pack still seeded |

New files: 4 `.scenario.ts` + one shared helper (`_helpers/first-run-onboarding.ts`). No first-run behavior or question wording changed.

## Why / how it works

First-run is **conductor-driven, not model-invocable** — there is no planner action the model can select to seed it; the affordance only reaches the model through `firstRunProvider`. So each scenario **splits the proof**:

- **Live message turns** exercise the model with the onboarding affordance surfaced (recorded trajectory = the "walk the user through" evidence). The seed step restores fresh `pending` state, since `createScenarioRuntime` force-marks first-run `complete`.
- A **custom final check owns pass/fail** by driving the real `FirstRunService` through the **production scheduled-task runner** — the same seam the in-chat conductor uses — then asserting `app_lifeops.life_scheduled_tasks` via `LifeOpsRepository`. This is the DOMAIN artifact ("outcome, not routing"), never chat text.

The conversational layer is deliberately **not** judged: because first-run isn't model-driven, the improvised replies vary widely run-to-run (see trajectories below), so gating on them would be flaky and would not prove the contract. The deterministic domain check is the contract.

Closes #14353

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] 4+ scenarios covering fast-start, full customize, resume-after-abandon, and channel-fallback — **authored + verified live**.
- [x] Final checks assert seeded `ScheduledTask` records (ids from `DEFAULT_PACK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEYS`) with anchors **derived from the answered wake time** — outcome, not routing.
- [x] Resume scenario proves no re-asking of already-answered questions (fresh `FirstRunService` resumes at `categories`).
- [x] No changes to question wording or first-run behavior.

> Note on record-ids: `FirstRunService.runDefaultsPath`/`runCustomizePath` seed the **first-run defaults pack** (`buildDefaultsPack` → `DEFAULT_PACK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEYS`, cron-anchored to the wake time), which is the code path onboarding actually exercises — asserted here. The separately-seeded `daily-rhythm` pack (boot seeder / spine registry) is disabled in the scenario runtime and is out of scope for these onboarding paths.

<details><summary>Domain-artifact assertions (what the custom checks verify against the real store)</summary>

The helper drives `FirstRunService` with `getScheduledTaskRunner(...)` (production runner) and reads back via `LifeOpsRepository.listScheduledTasks(agentId, { source: "first_run" })`:

71:Td7c,## Problem

Trajectory recording can attribute an outcome to the FINAL prompt but cannot decompose that prompt into provider contributions — the single fact blocking any learned optimization of context composition (provider selection/order/rendering/budgets) and any per-provider cost/win accounting. Provider accesses are logged length-only; the joined providers block sits undifferentiated inside the recorded prompt string; provider order is computed in-memory and never persisted.

## Current state (refs, worktree-verified)

- `logProviderAccess` records `data: { textLength }` only (`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4273`); `TrajectoryProviderAccessRecord` (`packages/core/src/services/trajectory-types.ts:130`) has no text, hash, or token count.
- `state.data.providerOrder` exists in-memory (`runtime.ts:4377`, consumed at `:7883-7890`) but is never stamped onto the recorded LLM call.
- No span offsets map prompt regions back to providers; no tokenizer pass over provider text; no (provider -> cost, marginal delta-judgeScore) ledger anywhere (`context-audit.ts` audits only context-category mapping; `recordInferenceSpan` captures latency only).
- The access LIST is already complete: while a trajectory step records, provider-cache reuse is disabled so every requested provider re-executes (`runtime.ts:4149-4164`) — capture fidelity is not the problem, record shape is.
- Everything else per call is already captured (full prompt, messages, tools, usage, costUsd — `runtime/trajectory-recorder.ts`; DB twin `trajectory-types.ts:85`), and judge rewards ride into datasets (`metadata.judge_score`, #8795).

## Proposed

1. Extend the provider-access record with `{ sha256, tokenCount, position, spanStart, spanEnd }` (text itself optional/hash-first to keep privacy-filter semantics; spans reference the recorded prompt string of the consuming call).
2. Stamp `providerOrder` (and the applied selection set) onto each `RecordedModelCall`/`TrajectoryLlmCallRecord` produced from that composeState.
3. Tokenizer pass at record time (same tokenizer family the batcher uses) for per-provider `tokenCount`; roll into a per-provider cost ledger derivable from existing `costUsd`.
4. Composition-aware replay groundwork: with spans + order persisted, a replay harness can re-render candidate (selection, order, template, budget) configs against recorded provider state — the inner loop for the GEPA-over-dynamic-context issue; `packages/scripts/trajectory.ts` gains a `providers` view (per-provider tokens/cost per call).
5. Keep the recording gate semantics unchanged (`runtime/trajectory-gate.ts`); size impact bounded by hash-first storage.

## Acceptance criteria + evidence bar

- A live recorded trajectory (scenario-runner, real model, read by hand) shows per-provider `{sha256, tokenCount, position, spanStart, spanEnd}` on each LLM call, and slicing the recorded prompt by the spans reproduces each provider's text exactly (round-trip test).
- `trajectory.ts` prints a per-provider token/cost table for a real trajectory; provider set + order reconstructable from the record alone (fixture test over a multi-provider compose).
- No behavior change when trajectory logging is off; privacy filter still strips provider text where required (hash retained).

## Out of scope

The optimizer/genome work and the ablation runner (parent GEPA issue); report rendering (reports issue); DB schema migrations beyond the trajectory record shape.
72:Tb2a,Part of #14878

## Problem

Parent: [her-tasks] Executive/creative agent task catalog (family 4). The corpus has zero creative-output scenarios (no draft/essay/naming/deck task anywhere in `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/test/scenarios/`; lifeops-bench mail.py covers triage, not composition-as-craft). Two capabilities are missing for the Samantha-as-collaborator register: (1) a voice-memo -> transcript -> structured-draft pipeline that preserves affect ("keep the anger in the second one"), and (2) owner-voice fidelity ("my voice, not consultant voice", "sound like me on a good day").

## Current state (refs)

- Media plumbing exists: content-addressed store (`packages/agent/src/api/media-store.ts`), SEARCH_KNOWLEDGE media-format facets (`packages/agent/src/actions/knowledge.ts:341-356`), whisper STT via plugin-local-inference. Not composed into memo->essay.
- Owner-voice ground truth exists but is unused for style: sent mail, prior essays/threads in knowledge, OwnerFactStore. Nothing builds a style profile or conditions drafting on it.
- Multi-turn iterative critique works mechanically (planner loop, multi-turn scenarios supported by scenario-runner) — untested for creative persistence; Tier-A riff/critique tasks in the parent cover that without new capability.
- Optimization hook: a `creative_draft` OptimizedPromptTask slot would let DSPy/GEPA artifacts tune drafting per-owner later (`packages/core/src/services/optimized-prompt.ts:67-108` pattern).

## Proposed

1. Memo->essay pipeline: ingest audio memos (store + STT + knowledge index with per-memo affect notes), then a composition flow that drafts against the transcripts, preserving per-memo tone directives; output lands as a document artifact, iterable in-thread.
2. Owner-voice profile: build a style card from owner-authored corpus (sent mail, prior essays) — diction, cadence, stance markers — injected as a provider when a task requests "my voice"; refreshed as corpus grows.
3. Iteration contract: revisions operate on the standing draft artifact (not regenerate-from-scratch), tracking owner vetoes across turns.
4. Judged voice-fidelity eval: judge compares candidate vs owner-corpus exemplars vs a deliberately generic baseline; scenario passes only when the candidate is closer to the exemplars.

## Acceptance criteria + evidence bar

- Live scenarios: (a) two seeded voice memos (one angry) -> essay retaining the seeded arguments and the anger in the mapped section, verified by judge rubric; (b) Series B narrative + launch thread scored closer to seeded owner exemplars than to the generic baseline; (c) multi-turn revision preserves prior accepted edits.
- Draft artifacts, style card, and trajectories inspected by hand.

## Out of scope

TTS/voice output; fine-tuning weights on owner text (APOLLO lane); image/deck rendering (narrative text only).
73:T1851,Part of the corpus PII scrub pipeline (multimodal foundation) — and a standalone knowledge-hub improvement.

## Problem

Transcripts already mirror into knowledge and are chunked/embedded like documents, but the mirror is `transcriptPlainText()` (`packages/shared/src/transcripts.ts`), which STRIPS all timing; fragments inherit `transcriptId`/`audioUrl` but have no per-fragment time range. Consequences:

- A search hit cannot seek the stored audio — the player opens at t=0.
- The PII pipeline cannot map a text-PII span found in a fragment back to an audio timestamp span, which `[pii] Audio redaction` requires.
- **Live data-loss bug (prerequisite):** voice-session WAVs are invisible to the media GC. `transcriptKnowledgePayload` sets ONLY `metadata.audioUrl` (`plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/transcript-knowledge.ts:66`) while `collectReferencedMedia` scans only `content.attachments[].url`/`thumbnailUrl` + `metadata.mediaUrl` (`packages/agent/src/api/media-runtime.ts:161-193`), so the WAV is swept after the 1h grace on the next daily `MEDIA_GC`. `meeting-transcript-writer.ts:425-432` documents this exact hazard and sets BOTH keys; the voice-session path does not. Timestamps into deleted audio are meaningless.

Producer fidelity today: local fused eliza-1-asr ABI v12 gives per-word ms spans (`asrTranscribeTimed`, `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/ffi-bindings.ts:395/918/2193`); meeting segments carry `words: []` because the seam is the locked string-only `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION` (`plugins/plugin-meetings/src/pipeline/transcriber.ts` header documents why); the cloud STT route parses only `{text}` and discards all timestamps (`packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/stt/route.ts`).

## Architecture

1. **Pre-chunked ingest seam:** optional `fragments?: Array<{text, metadata: {segmentIds, startMs, endMs, speakerLabels}}>` input on `DocumentService.addDocument` (`packages/core/src/features/documents/service.ts:645`) / `processFragmentsSynchronously` (`packages/core/src/features/documents/document-processor.ts:95`). `fragmentMetadata` already spreads document metadata, so per-fragment `startMs`/`endMs` rides jsonb metadata — zero schema/table change.
2. **Producers chunk on segment boundaries:** `transcriptKnowledgePayload` (`plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/transcript-knowledge.ts`) and `plugins/plugin-meetings/src/transcripts/meeting-transcript-writer.ts` build ~chunk-size groups from `Transcript.segments` they already hold — never splitting inside a segment.
3. **Project anchors through search:** `/api/documents/search` result mapping (`plugins/plugin-documents/src/routes.ts:785`) adds `transcriptId`, `startMs`, `endMs` next to `documentId`/`position`; same for the `documents` action=search formatter (`packages/core/src/features/documents/actions.ts`) so agent-facing hits carry anchors.
4. **Deep-link playback:** `packages/ui/src/components/pages/documents-detail.tsx` / TranscriptPlayer accept an initial seek (`?t=<ms>` or prop); `flattenTranscriptWords`/`activeWordIndex` already exist — only the entry offset is missing.
5. **GC fix (prerequisite):** set `metadata.mediaUrl = audioUrl` in `transcriptKnowledgePayload` (matching the meeting writer) AND/OR make `collectReferencedMedia` also collect `metadata.audioUrl`.
6. **Producer fidelity (second priority within this issue):**
   - Meetings word timings: expose timed ASR as a real runtime seam — a service or additive typed model registration in plugin-local-inference wrapping `transcribePcmTimed`/`asrTranscribeTimed` — so plugin-meetings' `AsrBackend` can return `words[]` when the fused v12 lib serves. Do NOT widen the locked `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION` ⇒ string contract; add a parallel typed surface.
   - Cloud STT timestamps: `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/stt/route.ts` requests `response_format=verbose_json` (+ `timestamp_granularities` where the deployed faster-whisper supports it), parses segments/words, and returns them in the DTO alongside `transcript`.
7. **Edits stay correct for free:** `TranscriptService.update` already deletes + re-adds the mirror; segment-boundary chunking re-derives anchors from patched segments.
8. **Documented caveat, not fixed here:** v12 word timings are duration-proportional char-weighted, not forced alignment — sufficient for seek/highlight anchors; `validateAsrWordTimings` (`packages/shared/src/transcripts.ts`) remains the producer gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fragment rows for a mirrored transcript carry `startMs`/`endMs`/`segmentIds`; boundaries never split a segment (unit + integration against real fixture audio — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/native/audio-fixtures/freeman.wav`, harness pattern `asr-timed.real.test.ts`).
- `/api/documents/search` and the `documents` action return `transcriptId` + `startMs` + `endMs`; UI evidence: MP4 walkthrough — search a word, click the hit, the player opens mid-audio at the anchor and the word is audible.
- **GC regression test:** seeded voice-session transcript + WAV → run the referenced-set computation → WAV survives; the test FAILS on current develop behavior.
- Meetings: with the fused v12 lib present, meeting segments carry `words[]` (`*.real.test.ts` lane, skipped-never-faked when the lib/bundle is absent); cloud STT DTO carries segments/words (live contract test precedent: `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/voice-kokoro-whisper-live.test.ts`).
- Transcript edit → re-mirror recomputes anchors (test patches a segment, asserts new fragment ranges).
- Evidence inline in the PR: fragment row dumps, search JSON, deep-link playback video, GC logs (`PR_EVIDENCE.md`).

## Out of scope

The PII scrub itself; audio muting (`[pii] Audio redaction`); any second file store or files/refcount table (#8876); whisper.cpp resurrection (retired — fused eliza-1-asr only); widening `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION`.

## Pipeline integration

This is the multimodal pipeline's text↔time bridge: the LLM-pass finds PII in fragment text; fragment anchors + word timings convert verdicts to timestamp spans consumed by `[pii] Audio redaction`. Fragments are documents, so the corpus enumeration and `pii:<sha256>:v<ruleset>` idempotency layers apply unchanged.
74:T1809,Part of the corpus PII scrub pipeline — extends it to audio. Depends on `[pii] Transcript fragments with time anchors` (anchors + the audioUrl GC fix).

## Problem

Text scrubbing leaves PII audible in stored recordings (voice sessions, meetings). Needed: word-timestamp-aligned muting/bleeping that preserves duration (so every transcript anchor stays valid), a redacted variant stored as a second content-addressed object — original for OWNER/ADMIN, redacted for everyone else, composing with the permissioning epic — and a re-transcribe-verify loop proving the PII is actually inaudible.

## Architecture

- **Span production:** timed ASR per-word `{text, startMs, endMs}` via `eliza_inference_asr_transcribe_timed` (ABI v12 — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/ffi-bindings.ts:395/918/1515/2193`, `timedAsrSupported()` gate; real-audio contract test `asr-timed.real.test.ts`). Text-PII verdicts from the LLM-pass over anchored transcript fragments merge onto word spans → `[{startMs, endMs}]` with padding. Pseudonym labels for spans come from the corpus map (`[pii] Context-retrieval pass`) so audio and text redaction agree on identity.
- **Mute op (empirically verified on ffmpeg 8.1.1):** `ffmpeg -i in -af "volume=0:enable='between(t,S1,E1)+between(t,S2,E2)+...'" -c:a <codec> out` — spans compose by summing `between()` terms. Bleep variant: `-f lavfi -i "sine=f=1000"` + `filter_complex` `amix duration=first`. Measured: WAV → exact duration, −91 dB true silence in span; OGG/opus → exact; M4A/AAC → +1 trailing encoder frame — assert duration with ±(1024/sampleRate)s tolerance or normalize through WAV. Sample count within the stream never changes, so span coordinates remain valid in the redacted variant.
- **Runtime capability:** ffmpeg is desktop/server-only (`packages/agent/src/runtime/core-plugins.ts:168`, `packages/core/src/runtime-env.ts:410` — iOS/Android/workers have none); probe like `whichBin('ffmpeg')` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/mic-source.ts`. The voice pipeline's native format is 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV (`ASR_SAMPLE_RATE`), so pure-TS PCM sample zeroing covers WAV with no ffmpeg at all; ffmpeg is the lane for lossy formats. Hosted option: a `media-redact` Railway sibling of `packages/cloud/services/voice-whisper-stt` (same Dockerfile/railway.toml/live-test pattern) — workerd cannot run ffmpeg, cloud-api may only orchestrate.
- **Storage (#8876-clean):** redacted bytes → `persistMediaBytes` (`packages/agent/src/api/media-store.ts:291`) → new sha256 object at `${STATE_DIR}/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`, served at `/api/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`. No new store, no files table, no fileId. Additive optional `Media` field only (sanctioned by the additive-widening block at `packages/core/src/types/primitives.ts:243-249`), e.g. `redactedOf?: string` (source sha) or `variant?: "redacted"`.
- **Permissioning (composes with the epic):** media bytes are served pre-auth — the sha256 is the capability — so enforcement lives at REFERENCE DISTRIBUTION, not the serve path: the transcript/document DTO carries the ORIGINAL sha URL only for `Role.OWNER`/`ADMIN` (`packages/core/src/types/environment.ts:43-51`; `packages/agent/src/api/boundary-role-resolver.ts`), the redacted sha for everyone else; the original hash must never enter non-privileged message records/context. GC: `gcUnreferencedMedia` (`media-store.ts:503`) keeps each variant alive only while referenced.
- **Re-transcribe-verify loop:** redacted bytes → `runtime.useModel(ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION, {audio, transcriptionPurpose: "interim"})` (`TranscriptionParams`, `packages/core/src/types/model.ts:940-952`; local handler = fused eliza-1-asr; `AsrUnavailableError` ⇒ the verify step FAILS, never a vacuous pass) → assert (a) every PII token ABSENT — exact + normalized fuzzy match, NOT transcript equality (Whisper-family models hallucinate filler over silence), and (b) sentinel non-PII words still PRESENT (over-mute guard). Cloud variant: POST the redacted file to voice-whisper-stt `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- Text-side precedent: trajectory redaction (`packages/agent/src/runtime/trajectory-internals.ts:1304` `redactTrajectoryParams`).

## Acceptance criteria

- E2E on real audio: fixture WAV (freeman.wav or a purpose-recorded fixture with planted PII) → spans → mute AND bleep variants across wav/ogg/m4a; per-codec duration assertions; `volumedetect` proves ≤ −85 dB in muted windows.
- **Redacted-audio artifact opened and LISTENED to by a human** — attach the redacted audio inline in the PR (MP4) with a note of what was heard. Hard evidence gate.
- Re-transcribe-verify test in the `*.real.test.ts` lane (skipped-never-faked when `ELIZA_INFERENCE_LIBRARY`/`ELIZA_ASR_BUNDLE` absent): PII absent, sentinels present; a deliberately broken run (one span omitted) FAILS the verify.
- Role test: OWNER DTO carries the original URL; USER/GUEST DTO carries only the redacted URL; a scan proves the original sha never appears in non-privileged room records.
- GC test: both variants referenced → both survive; original dereferenced (retention state flipped) → original collected, redacted survives.
- Idempotency: same input sha + same spans + same ruleset version ⇒ identical output sha; the pipeline done-marker makes re-runs no-ops.
- Constrained-runtime behavior: without ffmpeg, WAV redaction still works (pure-TS zeroing) and lossy-format redaction fails observably (typed error via `runtime.reportError`), never silently skipped.

## Out of scope

Video/image redaction; live/streaming redaction; any files/refcount table (#8876); serve-path auth changes (the capability model stands); forced-alignment ASR upgrades (char-weighted timing is the documented baseline).

## Pipeline integration

Extends the corpus pipeline to multimodal: LLM-pass verdicts (with corpus-consistent pseudonym labels from the context pass) become timestamp spans via the transcript-anchor issue; execution rides `[pii] Async scrub job rails` and the shared `pii:<sha256>:v<ruleset>` idempotency layer; the variant swap is the audio analog of the text write-back stage.

3. Wire the marker retirement path: share/download/delete unified with the Files surface per #8876 AD-completeness(2) (`TRANSCRIPT_MARKER` round-trip at `TranscriptViewerOverlay.tsx:54` slated for retirement) — do the transcript-share part here, full unification tracked in #8876 follow-ups.

- Variant determinism test (same transcript → same surrogates); original + chat copy + audio byte-identical after redaction.
- Actions respect roleGate; denied attempts audit-logged.

## Out of scope
Audio waveform redaction, consent ENFORCEMENT, UI (PERM-UX).

## What changed

**1. The floating boot pill is gone entirely.** `BootStatusIndicator` ("Waking …" / "… is taking longer than usual to wake") and its grace/escalation timers are deleted from `ContinuousChatOverlay`. Boot state has no surface above the chat.

**2. The floating `CloudHandoffBanner` toast is gone too.** The shared→dedicated handoff keeps its durable home-grid tile (`agent-provisioning`), and failures now speak in the transcript (below).

**3. Boot trouble is an agent chat message with buttons.** New headless `use-boot-recovery-conductor` (mirrors the existing model-status conductor): when a boot stalls past 90 s or a dedicated-agent handoff fails/times out, it seeds ONE assistant turn (`boot:recovery`) into the live transcript with a **specific** diagnosis and remedy:
   - Eliza Cloud session unusable → *"…your Eliza Cloud session looks signed out."* → **Re-log in** (drives `handleCloudLogin`) + Try again
   - session fine, agent unresponsive → **Try again** (drives `triggerRestart`) + Re-log in
   - handoff failed/timed out → *"I couldn't finish setting up your dedicated agent…"* → **Retry setup** (re-dispatches the handoff supervisor)
   - missing local model was already covered in-chat by the model-status conductor (**Download now** / **Use Eliza Cloud instead**) — unchanged.
   Controls ride a reserved `__boot_recovery__:` value prefix consumed by the send funnel (never reaches the server); the card updates in place, returns its controls after an action settles (no dead-end "Reconnecting…" states), removes itself the moment the agent is healthy, and never renders during onboarding (first-run conductor owns that screen) or the no-provider state (the transcript's no-provider gate owns it).

**4. No chat suggestions anywhere.** The FTU welcome dashboard widget (greeting + "try saying…" chips), the resting composer suggestion strip, `usePromptSuggestions`, and the now-consumerless `POST /api/suggestions` server route are all deleted. The agent is proactive; canned prompts are gone.

**5. Onboarding is truly full-screen, then settles to half.** The content-sizing seam that shrank the pinned onboarding sheet is removed — onboarding owns the whole screen. On the completion edge the sheet **springs FULL → HALF** (was: collapse) in step with the opaque-backdrop fade, so the home appears behind the top half while the conversation stays in hand.

**6. Cloud-only onboarding confirmed unchanged** — the runtime chooser stays default-off everywhere (`first-run-runtime-flag.ts`), sign-in to Eliza Cloud is the single path.

7c:Tc53,## Notification shade rework

Reworks the home notification surface per product direction. Six changes:

1. **No card chrome.** The inbox floats on the shade's surface — no fill, no border, no blur of its own (`HOME_GLASS_CLASS` dropped from `NotificationsHomeCenter`).
2. **Bulk clear-all removed.** The header trash button is gone; notifications are dismissed one at a time.
3. **Pointer-idiomatic per-row dismiss.** A mouse reveals an **X on hover/focus**; touch **throws the row left or right** past a threshold to dismiss (springs back below it).
4. **Gesture inverted.** The shade now **drops DOWN** from a top hint — or from a **downward drag anywhere** on the home when scrolled to top — and **drags UP to hide**. This is the inverse of the chat sheet, which rises from the bottom.
5. **Pull-down collapses chat.** Revealing the shade fires a new `CHAT_COLLAPSE_EVENT`, wired into `ContinuousChatOverlay` (`goToDetent("collapsed")`, gated off during onboarding).
6. **Tap → view, or contextual menu.** Tap opens the deep-linked view; a **long-press (touch) / right-click (mouse)** opens a contextual menu (open / mark read / dismiss).

### Files (notification rework)
- `NotificationsHomeCenter.tsx` — borderless card, row swipe + hover-X + long-press/right-click menu, `onMarkRead` prop, clear-all removed.
- `NotificationsShade.tsx` — top-anchored slide-down sheet with an up-drag-to-close grabber.
- `HomeScreen.tsx` — top pull-down hint (ChevronDown), region-wide downward-drag reveal, `openShade` collapses chat, listens for `OPEN_NOTIFICATION_CENTER_EVENT`.
- `ContinuousChatOverlay.tsx` / `events/index.ts` — `CHAT_COLLAPSE_EVENT` + `dispatchChatCollapse()`.

### Tests
- Updated unit tests: `NotificationsHomeCenter.test.tsx` (borderless card, no clear-all, context-menu dismiss), `HomeScreen.test.tsx` (downward pull opens shade, region drag collapses chat), `NotificationsHomeCenter.render-count.test.tsx` (`onMarkRead` in `rowPropsEqual`).
- Updated app e2e `gesture-matrix.spec.ts`: the removed clear-all path is replaced with the per-row context-menu dismiss.
- `bun run --cwd packages/ui test <shell specs>` → **34 passed**. Typecheck + biome clean on all touched files (remaining repo-wide lint/tsc errors are pre-existing, in files this PR does not touch).

### Evidence
- ⚠️ **Visual/e2e capture pending** — the gesture flow needs the local Playwright recipe (`packages/app audit:app` / the `gesture-matrix` spec). Unit coverage proves the wiring; rendered before/after screenshots + a video walkthrough should be attached before merge.

## v2 — per-auth-path intake, layered env, committed evidence ledger

v2 rebuilds the dashboard around **auth paths instead of connector families**: every family is a section with one sub-row per way it can authenticate (36 paths across 15 families from the `CONNECTOR_PATHS` registry, `scripts/lifeops/connector-paths.mjs`), each with its own env slots, availability verdict, live probe, freshness badge, and — where possible — a one-click acquisition. Feature issues: #14791 (auth-path matrix), #14792 (one-click logins), #14794 (evidence ledger + freshness), #14795 (OWNER/AGENT slots), #14799 (free-probe catalog).

**Features**

- **Layered env resolution** (`scripts/lifeops/env-layers.mjs`): `process.env` > worktree `.env` > **main-checkout `.env`** (git-discovered via `rev-parse --git-common-dir`, linked worktrees only) > `~/.eliza/.env`. Every field renders its winning source layer badge; the header prints all four resolved file paths. The dashboard never mutates `process.env`, so badges stay truthful after saves.
- **Saves** default to `~/.eliza/.env` (created on demand, atomic tmp+rename, mode 600 — survives worktree churn) with a per-save toggle for the repo `.env`. Writes are allowlisted to the 68 registry env names; `WRITE_ALIASES` keeps divergent spellings in sync (`ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY`↔`ELIZA_CLOUD_API_KEY`, `ELIZA_WHATSAPP_*`↔`WHATSAPP_*`). POSTs are loopback-only + same-origin + per-process session token.
- **One-clicks:** GitHub token reuse from the `gh` CLI keyring (server-side, saved masked), headless SIWE login against real Eliza Cloud (`scripts/cloud/siwe-test-login.mjs`), `signal-cli link` pairing-URI emission, and deep-links into the app's own OAuth flows.
- **OWNER/AGENT identity slots** (matrix states 2/3/6): `github.pat` carries real env slots (`GITHUB_USER_PAT`/`GITHUB_AGENT_PAT` + `ELIZA_E2E_*` fallbacks, `rolesVia: env-slots`); Google/X roles ride OAuth `metadata.requestedRole` or separate real accounts per the owner-agent matrix doc §3 (`rolesVia` encodes which).
- **Committed evidence ledger** `docs/testing/hitl-ledger.json` (`scripts/lifeops/hitl-ledger.mjs`): per path `{pathId, lastSuccessAt, lastRunAt, lane, commit, counts:{passed,failed,skipped}}`, stable-sorted, atomic writes, never secrets. Freshness bands (locked): **green ≤7d, yellow >7d, red >30d-or-never**, computed from `lastSuccessAt`.
- **Lane driver v2** (`scripts/lifeops/run-11632-live-lanes.mjs`): hydrates the same layered env, gates per auth path, upserts + auto-commits the ledger per lane, `--status` renders the freshness table, `--dry-run` lists per-path readiness incl. suiteless paths.

**How to run**

```bash
bun run lifeops:hitl                                  # dashboard (loopback, port-walks from 43117; --open to launch browser)
node scripts/lifeops/run-11632-live-lanes.mjs --status   # ledger freshness table
node scripts/lifeops/run-11632-live-lanes.mjs --dry-run  # per-path readiness + SKIP reasons
node scripts/lifeops/run-11632-live-lanes.mjs            # run all ready live lanes
```

- `github.user-oauth`: no in-repo public OAuth client id exists, so a local device-code flow can't be offered — skip-with-reason until an org OAuth app ships (#14792).
- `discord.user-oauth`: the in-tree exchange (`packages/app-core/src/api/auth/discord-exchange.ts`) is Activity-iframe-only; a user-OAuth one-click needs a Discord org app (#14792).
- `google.oauth-owner`/`google.oauth-agent`: need `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`/`GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` (org OAuth app); the one-click is a deep-link into the app's own connector flow (#14792).
- `x.agent-account`: permanently `skip` by design — the agent's X identity is a separate real account (owner-agent matrix doc §3), not an env slot.
- `x.bearer-app` proves the bearer is alive but `users/me` returns an honest 403 (app-only auth forbidden there); user-context X needs the OAuth1 tuple (`TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`_SECRET`).
- `signal.cli` link on this machine surfaces a real Java `LinkageError` (signal-cli built for class-file 69 vs JRE 65) as a 502 — environment defect, reported honestly, not masked.

80:T35f5,Implements the certification protocol from #14546 (epic #14541): verdict rollup, reviewer verdicts, Ed25519-signed `certification.json`, and fully-offline verification — the security-critical piece the develop→main CI gate (#14547) will call. Built on the `@elizaos/evidence` foundation from #14589 (merged).

> **Stacking note:** #14589 is merged into `develop`. This branch also carries the post-merge review-hardening commit from `feat/14552-evidence-bundle` (`c902a6a5fe6`: symlink-aware verify, `metaSha256` provenance binding, strict canonical objects, NFC paths) cherry-picked on top, because certification builds directly on those contracts. If that commit lands on `develop` through its own PR first, a rebase here dedupes it cleanly. **Consumed by #14547.**

## What + why

A pile of green lanes is not a promotion claim. This PR turns a finalized evidence bundle into a **signed, offline-verifiable statement**: *a keyholder reviewed exactly these verdicts over exactly this bundle for exactly this commit*. Everything the gate needs is in `packages/evidence` — the workflow in #14547 stays a thin caller with zero verification logic of its own.

New (ownership-scoped; additive-only outside `src/certify/**`):

- `src/certify/schema.ts` — strict certification contract (zod + frozen interfaces, mutually-assignable compile guards like the foundation).
- `src/certify/keys.ts` — node:crypto Ed25519 keygen, SPKI-DER sha256 fingerprints (first 16 hex), signing-key ingress (`ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` PEM or base64-wrapped PEM, or `--key-file`). Nothing here writes or logs a private key.
- `src/certify/rollup.ts` — mechanical draft verdicts from lane `result.json` counters, `analysis.json` expectation failures, and caller-declared requirements (honest-skip: skipped/absent lanes fail unless marked optional-with-reason, then draft as `waived` carrying the reason).
- `src/certify/sign.ts` — `signCertification` / `verifyCertification` with distinct typed failure codes; the report lists **all** detectable failures, never first-failure-only.
- `src/certify/cli.ts` + package scripts — `certify:keygen | rollup | sign | verify`.
- `.github/certification/` — trust-model README (base-branch key rule, rotation, break-glass) written explicitly for #14547 to implement. The public-key PEM is deliberately NOT in this PR: the key custodian lands the production key in a dedicated reviewed PR (merging it is the act of trusting the key).

## Certification schema (`schema: 1`)

```ts
{
  schema: 1,
  bundleSha: string,      // sha256 hex of the bundle's manifest.json bytes
  commit: string,         // full 40-hex sha — short shas rejected
  branch: string,
  baseRef: string,
  tier: 'cpu' | 'gpu' | 'full',
  verdicts: [{ subject, verdict: 'pass'|'fail'|'waived',
               evidence: string[] /* bundle-relative */, notes? }],
  reviewer: { kind: 'agent'|'human', id, model? },
  createdAt: string, expiresAt?: string,
  signature: { alg: 'ed25519', publicKeyFingerprint, value /* base64, 64 bytes */ }
}
```

Signature = Ed25519 over `canonicalJsonBytes(payload-without-signature)` (sorted keys, no whitespace, one trailing newline — the foundation's canonical form). Parsing is **strict**: unknown top-level fields, unknown verdict values, absolute/traversal evidence paths, duplicate subjects, empty verdict arrays, and `waived` without non-empty notes are all rejected. Forward compat is a `schema` bump, never silent tolerance.

## Threat model (summary — full text in `.github/certification/README.md`)

- **The gate MUST read the public key from the BASE branch (`main`), never the PR head** — otherwise one PR swaps key + self-signed cert together. Key rotation = a reviewed PR replacing the pem; merging it is the act of trusting the new key.
- A valid signature proves a keyholder signed these verdicts over this manifest for this commit. `bundleSha` binds the manifest; the foundation's `metaSha256` binds `meta.json` (commit/branch/tier source) transitively — forging provenance after signing surfaces as `bundle-tampered`.
- It does **not** prove diligence; the reviewer identity is inside the signed payload for exactly that reason, and the gate should surface it in the check summary.
- `wrong-key` (different keypair) is distinguished from `bad-signature` (altered payload); forging the trusted fingerprint on a foreign signature moves the failure to `bad-signature` — the crypto check still holds (tested).
- Break-glass is **not a code path**: admin bypass of the required check, visible in the GitHub audit log. There is deliberately no flag or env var that skips signature checks.
- `certify:sign` refuses to sign a bundle that fails integrity verification, and the verifier hard-errors (rather than reporting "cert invalid") on a misconfigured trusted key so an attacker cannot induce a misleading outcome.

## Verify contract for #14547

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/evidence certify:verify -- \
  --cert <certification.json> \
  --pubkey <BASE-branch>/.github/certification/certification-public-key.pem \
  --expected-commit <pr-head-sha> --max-age-hours 72 --required-tier full \
  [--bundle <dir>] --json
```

Exit `0` iff valid, `1` otherwise. `--json` prints the full `CertificationVerifyReport` on stdout: `{ ok, failures: [{code, message, context}], payload?, certification?, bundle? }` with codes `schema-invalid | unsigned | bad-signature | wrong-key | stale | commit-mismatch | bundle-tampered | verdict-failures | tier-insufficient`.

## Key custody note for the repo owner

No key material ships in this PR — neither half. The key custodian (repo owner) generates the production keypair on a trusted machine, stores the private half as the `ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` repo secret, and lands the public PEM (with its fingerprint) via a dedicated reviewed PR per `.github/certification/README.md`. Until then the gate (#14547) cannot be enabled; `certify:verify` has no default trust anchor and requires an explicit `--pubkey`.

Part of #14546 (protocol layer: `certify:keygen|rollup|sign|verify`). Still open on that issue: the unified `evidence:certify --tier` orchestrator entrypoint and the committed trust-anchor PEM.

81:T223e,## What + why

Adds the tiered heuristic **analyzer registry** to `packages/evidence` (#14542, epic #14541). An analyzer is a pure `(input, ctx) -> status-bearing fragment` that declares which artifact kinds it consumes and which tier (`cpu`/`gpu`) it belongs to. A runner fans every applicable analyzer over every visual subject in a bundle and writes ONE `analysis.json` per subject **beside its pixels**, with an honest per-analyzer status:

- `ran` — executed and produced data
- `skipped-tier` — analyzer tier above the run tier (e.g. gpu analyzer on a cpu run)
- `skipped-missing-tool` — required binary / endpoint / baseline unavailable
- `failed` — the analyze call threw (message captured; one broken analyzer can't fail the matrix)

No analyzer is silently dropped; no skip fabricates empty data (repo doctrine: "not loaded" must never read as "zero"). The registry is **data, not a plugin system** — a flat array + name lookup, no dynamic loading.

The four `visual-qa.mjs` primitives (OCR, palette, brand-rule fractions, size-agnostic change-metric) are ported with behaviour preserved and real tests added; the missing cheap heuristics from the issue are implemented.

> **Stacked on #14589** (foundation, merged to develop) and its post-review hardening commit on `feat/14552-evidence-bundle` (merged in here). Mark ready + rebase once that hardening lands on develop. All **97 foundation tests stay green** alongside the **39 new analyzer tests** (136 total).

## Analyzers

| name | tier | consumes (kinds) | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ocr.tesseract` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | `{ engine, text, words, confidence }` (ported; `skipped-missing-tool` when tesseract absent) |
| `ocr.unlimited` | gpu | screenshot, keyframe | same shape via OpenAI-compatible `llama-server` (Baidu Unlimited-OCR, #14543); endpoint `ELIZA_GPU_VISION_URL`, `skipped-missing-tool` when unset/unreachable |
| `color.palette` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | dominant-k quantized swatches `{ hex, rgb, fraction }` (ported) |
| `color.corners` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | 4-corner + centre swatches `{ position, rgb, hex, bucket }` — wrong-theme / dark-mode bleed |
| `brand.rules` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | blue/orange/neutral fractions + brand verdict (orange-accent-only, no-blue) (ported) |
| `diff.change` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | size-agnostic change fraction + bbox (ported); baseline via `ctx.baselineResolver` |
| `diff.region` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | pixelmatch -> clustered changed-region bboxes `[{x,y,w,h,fraction}]` + per-region change/static assertions |
| `hash.perceptual` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | 64-bit DCT pHash + Hamming/same-screen utils (no new dep — computed on sharp raw) |
| `tree.aria` | cpu | html-tree | node count + normalized snapshot; pure `normalize`/`diff`/`prune` exports (no Playwright dep) |
| `video.keyframes` | cpu | video | ffmpeg scene-cut + first/last frames -> emits `keyframe` artifacts under `video/keyframes/<slug>/`; image analyzers then fan over them |

**Engine indirection** (`OcrEngine = { id, available(), recognize() }`) lets one analyzer body serve tesseract, the gpu `unlimited` client, and `apple-vision`. The **Apple Vision** helper (`packages/app/scripts/ocr-vision.swift`, PR #14490) is merged in develop and wrapped as `AppleVisionOcrEngine` (macOS + swift, stdin NDJSON); it is exported but not yet in the default registry pending the consumer-migration follow-up (#14470).

**New dep:** `pixelmatch@^7` (was already a transitive dep). `sharp@^0.34.5` (repo-standard) added explicitly. Both appended to `package.json` without reordering existing keys.

## What & why

Agent-invoked **VLM screenshot Q&A** in `packages/evidence`: a reviewing agent (claude/codex) generates targeted questions about a screenshot and gets **structured** answers back — the semantic layer (blue-fraction, OCR, diff regions) can't answer "is the Send button clipped?" or "is this the designed empty state or a blank panel?". Answers land in `qa.json` beside the pixels with full model + token-usage provenance so the certify reviewer (#14546) folds them into verdicts.

Runs **standalone in minimal containers** — no dependency on `@elizaos/*` plugin packages. Talks to the model APIs by direct `fetch` (the plugin conventions were read for the wire shapes, not imported).

### Design points
- **One request per image carrying ALL questions** — image tokens paid once; response forced to strict JSON `{answers:[{id,answer,confidence,details}]}`.
- **Strict parsing, no regex rescue.** A non-conforming response throws `VISION_RESPONSE_INVALID`; exactly **one** corrective retry is spent (and counted in `provenance.retries`) before failing typed. Never a fabricated answer.
- **NOT_CONFIGURED is a typed failure, never a default.** No key / base URL / explicit backend ⇒ `VISION_NOT_CONFIGURED` (keyless-env contract: explicit skip, never invented answers).
- **Downscale longest edge → 1568px** via sharp before base64 (Anthropic downsamples past that anyway); original + sent dimensions recorded.
- **Content-addressed cache** at `<bundle|cwd>/.vision-qa-cache/<sha256(image)>/<sha256(model+backend+questions-canonical)>.json` using the foundation's `canonicalJson` for the query key; `--no-cache` bypass; corrupt entry ⇒ miss.

### Backends (one interface, `VisionBackendClient`)

| Backend | Transport | Model default | Image | Key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | Messages `/v1/messages` | `claude-opus-4-8` | base64 block | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openai` | chat.completions | `gpt-5.5` | `image_url` data-URI + `response_format: json_object` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `local` | chat.completions @ `ELIZA_VISION_QA_BASE_URL` | `qwen3-vl` | `image_url` data-URI | none (llama-server) |

`ELIZA_VISION_QA_BACKEND` ∈ `anthropic|openai|local`; default `anthropic` when key present, else `local` when base URL set, else NOT_CONFIGURED.

### Deliverables
- `askAboutImage(imagePath, questions, opts)` + `askBatch(entries, opts)` (inline p-limit, dependency-free; a per-entry failure rejects the batch — no silent drops). Anthropic Message-Batches API left as a documented seam, no stub.
- `suggestQuestions(analysis, {viewName?, expectations?})` — pure/deterministic; turns blue-over-threshold, large diff regions, and OCR dev-strings into targeted question drafts with stable ids.
- `writeQaRecord(bundle, subjectBundlePath, questions, askResult)` → kind `qa`, placed via `bundlePath` beside the subject (`visual/…/x.png` → `visual/…/x.qa.json`).
- CLI: `bun run --cwd packages/evidence vision-qa -- ask <image> -q "…" [--context analysis.json] [--backend …] [--json]` — `--context` runs `suggestQuestions` and merges ahead of `-q`.

### Foundation contract (absorbed the #14589 review-hardening)
Rebased onto `c902a6a5fe6` (symlink-aware verify, `metaSha256` provenance binding, strict-canonical objects). Impact confirmed: `writeQaRecord` builds plain-object/ISO-string records (`canonicalJson` no longer accepts Date/Map/class instances — pinned by a test), copies via `addArtifact` (no symlinks), and my `qa-record` test's `verifyBundle` still passes clean under the new verify.

83:T178e,Part of #14545 and epic #14541. This PR adds the video evidence lane infrastructure, but it does not close #14545 by itself: the remaining acceptance work is a real booted-app `--base-url` run and device-producer ingestion evidence through the same path.

## What changed

- Adds `packages/evidence/src/video/**` with MP4 normalization, video ingest, keyframe analysis fan-out, a data-driven Playwright walkthrough driver, schema validation, fixture server, shipped walkthrough definitions, and `video:walkthrough` / `video:ingest` CLIs.
- Treats video as first-class analyzed evidence: normalized clip, steps log, screenshots, ARIA snapshots, keyframes, and per-subject `analysis.json` all land in the bundle manifest.
- Keeps capture and analysis separated: Playwright is dynamically imported by walkthrough capture; pre-recorded video ingest does not need browser code.
- Resolves ffmpeg/ffprobe from explicit env, PATH, then installed static packages. It does not silently download/mutate dependencies at runtime; missing tools produce honest `skipped-missing-tool` records.
- Fixes OCR robustness exposed by this lane: Tesseract inputs are staged through a short temp path so deep bundle keyframe paths do not turn available OCR into failed analyzer records.
- Rebased onto current `develop`; the branch lands via squash merge as one clean commit.

## Review fixes

Addressed the blockers from earlier review comments:

- `steps=` now reports the actual executed walkthrough step count, not screenshots + ARIA count.
- If normalization is skipped because video tools are unavailable, ingest preserves the source extension instead of storing raw webm/mov bytes under `.mp4`.
- `waitFor.value` / `scroll.value` are numeric-string validated before they can reach Playwright as `NaN`.
- PR body language changed from closing #14545 to “Part of #14545” because fixture evidence is not the same as booted web/device evidence.
- The branch lands via squash merge, so intermediate commit metadata does not reach `develop`.

## What

New `packages/evidence` (`@elizaos/evidence`, private, ESM, no framework dependency — it must run in minimal CI/vast containers):

- **`src/schema.ts` — frozen schema-1 contract.** `ArtifactEntry` / `BundleManifest` / `BundleMeta` + `ArtifactKind`/`RunnerKind`/`Tier` unions, exactly as specced in the issue. Explicit interfaces are the contract; zod validators are held mutually assignable at compile time so type and validator cannot drift. Reading untrusted manifests/meta from disk throws `EvidenceValidationError` with per-field issues (error-policy J3) — never a silently-repaired object. Path traversal (`..`, absolute, backslash, `.`/empty segments) is rejected at validation time.
- **`src/canonical.ts` — signed byte form.** Canonical JSON: keys sorted (UTF-16 code-unit order), arrays in caller order, no whitespace, UTF-8, exactly one trailing newline (part of the signed bytes). Non-representable values (NaN/Infinity/bigint/function/undefined-in-array) throw instead of degrading to `null`.
- **`src/bundle.ts` — builder + verifier.** `createBundle` opens `evidence/runs/<utc yyyymmdd-hhmmss>-<shortsha>-<tier>/`; `addArtifact` hardlinks (same volume) or copies (EXDEV fallback, annotated J4), hashes **as stored**, and places by a deterministic kind→family mapping (`lanes/<lane>/…`, `visual/<source>/…`, `video/…`, `trajectories/…`, `html-trees/…`, `misc/<source>/…`) with a `bundlePath` escape hatch for wave-2 analyzers to sit `analysis.json`/`qa.json` beside pixels. `finalize()` sorts artifacts by path and writes canonical `manifest.json` + `meta.json`, returning `manifestSha256` (the value certification signs). `verifyBundle(dir)` re-hashes everything and reports `missing` / `size-mismatch` / `hash-mismatch` / `unlisted` findings. Clock and runId are injectable → byte-stable manifests are testable. Bundle paths are NFC-normalized at ingress (macOS NFD vs linux NFC). `finalize()` writes+hashes `meta.json` first and embeds `manifest.metaSha256`, binding provenance into the signed envelope; `verifyBundle` is lstat-based and additionally reports `symlink` (symlinked artifact = mutable after signing; symlinked dir = unswept external tree) and `meta-mismatch` findings.
- **`src/provenance.ts`.** Commit/branch via `git rev-parse` (execFile, fails loud with a typed error outside a repo — no fabricated provenance); runner from `ELIZA_EVIDENCE_RUNNER` ∈ local|vast|ci (invalid value throws instead of downgrading), inferred `ci` from `CI` env, default `local`; env fingerprint is a small allowlist (node/bun versions, platform, arch, tier, TEST_LANE) — full env is never captured.
- **`src/ingest.ts` — 7 silo ingestors, producers untouched.** e2e-recordings, aesthetic-audit-output, device-e2e-output (both roots; the #14494 bundle-dir shape), packages/app/test-results, reports/walkthrough (+ app mirror), reports/live-test-runs, scenario-runner reports (+ reports/scenarios). Roots mirror `scripts/evidence-review/generate.mjs` DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS. Each returns `{silo, status: 'ingested'|'absent', artifactCount}` — an absent silo and an empty silo are different results, never conflated.
- **`src/cli.ts` — thin.** `bundle:create -- --tier cpu|gpu|full [--out] [--repo-root]` and `bundle:verify -- <dir>`; all logic in the lib, J1 boundary translation at the process edge.
- Registered in the `server` test lane via `elizaos.scripts.testLanes` (verified in `run-all-tests.mjs --plan`).

## Schema contract summary (for wave-2 agents)

```ts
import {
  // schema
  ArtifactKind, RunnerKind, Tier, ArtifactEntry, BundleManifest, BundleMeta,
  ARTIFACT_KINDS, RUNNER_KINDS, TIERS, parseManifest, parseMeta, isBundleRelativePath,
  // bundle
  createBundle, EvidenceBundle, verifyBundle, formatRunId,
  // provenance
  collectGitProvenance, resolveRunnerKind, buildEnvFingerprint,
  // ingest
  ingestAllSilos, ingestNamedSilo, SILO_NAMES,
  // errors
  EvidenceError, EvidenceValidationError,
} from "@elizaos/evidence";
```

No deviations from the issue/spec schema. Two additions (additive, documented): `AddArtifactOptions.bundlePath` for exact placement (needed by #14542/#14544), and — from the fable review round — `BundleManifest.metaSha256` (required, 64-hex) binding `meta.json` bytes into the signed envelope so forged commit/branch/runner fails verification. Schema stays 1 (unreleased).

Deliberately **not** in this PR (hot-zone guard per the design doc — `scripts/evidence-review/**` has in-flight PRs): pointing `evidence-review/generate.mjs` at a bundle via `--bundle`. That lands with consolidation (#14550).

## What

`docker/certification/` runs the entire certification stack on one beefy Linux machine: container-parallel CPU test lanes + a pipelined GPU vision queue.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `compose.yml` | **Generated-then-committed** stack: `cpu` profile = one container per test lane with `cpuset` pinning + `cpus` quotas, read-only `/repo` mount, per-lane `scratch-*` volume, shared `build-cache`; `gpu` profile = one GPU-owning `gpu-vision` service (both resident llama-servers: Unlimited-OCR :8090 + Qwen3-VL :8091) + one `gpu-queue-worker` |
| `generate-compose-lanes.mjs` + `compose-lanes-lib.mjs` | Derives lane services from **`run-all-tests.mjs --plan=json --all`** — each `summary.byScript` script becomes a lane, big groups split with the runner's own `TEST_SHARD`, the plan's `cloudStep` becomes the `cloud` lane. **No second lane registry**; `--check` is the drift gate |
| `queue-lib.mjs` / `queue-worker.mjs` | Filesystem job queue (no redis/sqlite): claim-by-rename, max-pending backpressure on enqueue, drain-to-skip with honest `skipped` records once the GPU service is unreachable past a window. All state transitions pure + unit-tested |
| `certify-parallel.mjs` | Orchestrator: derive → `compose --profile cpu [--profile gpu] up` → per-lane exit codes/timings from `docker inspect` → `timings.json` whose `timings` field is `BundleMeta.timings`-compatible (`Record<phase, ms>`, packages/evidence). Deterministic degradation: no docker → serial fallback printed + **EXIT_NO_DOCKER=4**; compose drift → 5; timeout → 6 |
| `lane-entry.sh` / `gpu-entry.sh` | Container entrypoints (rsync-to-scratch + shared bun cache; dual llama-server launch that dies loudly if either server exits) |
| `README.md` | Cores→lane mapping, VRAM budget (~6–10 GiB both models at Q4), GPU-service-over-HTTP doctrine with **MPS as escape hatch only** (MIG N/A on consumer cards), macOS native-path pointer, queue protocol, exit codes |

Coordination with #14548: services **reference** `ghcr.io/elizaos/certification-gpu` (overridable via `ELIZA_CERT_IMAGE`/`ELIZA_CERT_GPU_IMAGE`); no competing Dockerfile is defined here.

CI: `bun test docker/certification` added to `scenario-pr.yml` (dir is outside workspace test discovery), covering the drift gate so `compose.yml` cannot silently diverge from the plan. `turbo.json` gains `ELIZA_CERT_QUEUE_HOST` in `globalEnv` (biome `noUndeclaredEnvVars`).

## What ships
- **Cloud launcher app** (`/cloud`, tile gated on cloud sign-in via `LAUNCHER_CLOUD_IDS`): credits + top-up, agents w/ live status (30s background poll that keeps last-good on blips), API keys + manage link, billing summary. Lean app-native view (dark launcher aesthetic), strict loading/signed-out/error/ready states, per-section designed degradation — never healthy-empty from a catch.
- **CLOUD_ACCOUNT provider** — `dynamic: true`, context-gated (cloud|settings|finance), ADMIN role-gated, 60s cache, stale-on-failure, signed-out → empty. **Zero context cost until the conversation actually touches cloud** (the context-layer routing), per the owner's requirement.
- **3 actions** — `CLOUD_ACCOUNT_STATUS`, `CLOUD_LIST_AGENTS`, `CLOUD_CREATE_API_KEY` — `validate()` gates on signed-in (they vanish signed-out); key creation shows the plain key once (never persisted in the ActionResult), refuses the reserved `agent-sandbox:` prefix, honest session-required replies.
- **`Plugin.packageName` seam** (core + views-registry): `name:"elizaOSCloud"` can't resolve its package dir for view bundles; the seam fixes it generically + test proves it.
- **`listCloudApiKeys`** client wrapper (packages/ui), typed not-connected/session-required reasons.

| `scripts/vast/run-certification.test.mjs` | 36 unit tests over the pure pieces (offer filter/sort, onstart assembly + 16 KB guard, poll state machine, budget guards, secret redaction, auth-error classification) — `bun run test:vast` |
| `scripts/vast/local-certify.mjs` | One-command local fallback: same chain, same signed output; `--no-sign` stops after rollup for hand review |
| `scripts/vast/README.md` | Runbook: local fallback, costs, kill-path table (one distinct exit code per kill path) |
| `docker/certification/Dockerfile.gpu` | Bakes CUDA `llama-server` (pinned llama.cpp `b8525`, the `scripts/gpu-vision` minimum), sha256-pinned OCR/VLM models via the repo's `setup.mjs --with-vlm`, Node 24, Bun 1.3.14, Playwright Chromium + deps, tesseract, ffmpeg — everything the 16 KB onstart cannot carry |
| `.github/workflows/certification-image.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` + develop-push path trigger; GHCR push via `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packages: write`); tags `latest` + `sha-<short>` |
| `.github/workflows/certification-vast.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` (sha/tier/max_dph/max_attempts/timeout inputs) + nightly cron gated on `vars.ELIZA_VAST_CERT_ENABLED == 'true'`; **no `pull_request` trigger**; secrets exposed only to the single run step; any failure goes red with a "local certification required: `node scripts/vast/local-certify.mjs --tier full`" summary |

## Design points

- **Secrets discipline:** `ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` + optional `CERT_PUSH_CMD` travel only in the create-payload env (docker `-e`), never in the onstart text, logs, or `--dry-run` output (unit-tested). The onstart is printable and safe.
- **Budget guards:** `--max-dph` (server-side `lte` + client-side re-check), `--max-attempts` across offers cheapest-first; retries fire only on host-side failures (stuck loading / instance lost / create rejected), never on chain failures or timeouts. Worst case per dispatch: `0.60 × 3 × 2h = $3.60`; each run logs its estimated spend.
- **Live-API verification without spend:** vast rejects a dead key with **HTTP 404 + `{"error":"auth_error"}`** (not 401), and search offers is `PUT /search/asks/` with a `{q: ...}` body (`select_cols: ["*"]` is rejected by the current API). Both discovered against the live API and encoded + unit-tested; the dead-key kill path is verified live below.
- **Results without storage:** the signed `certification.json` is emitted between log markers and recovered from the pulled instance logs, so a run is useful even before `ELIZA_CERT_PUSH_CMD` (R2/S3) is configured; the full bundle push stays env-driven.

8a:T22fb,Part of #14541. Implements the **evidence-side job queue** half of #14543 (the standalone GPU vision *service* landed in #14593; the analyzer registry with `ocr.unlimited` landed in #14611/#14958). This is the queue that lets capture lanes enqueue images as they appear and a resident GPU worker streams results back into `analysis.json`.

Not the `docker/certification` compose-level queue (#14964) — this is the in-package `@elizaos/evidence` queue.

## What this adds

- **`src/queue/state.ts`** — pure state machine (no fs/network/clock): job parse+validate (every defect listed, never a repaired default — J3), FIFO claim order over enqueue-timestamped ids, enqueue backpressure, the worker connectivity latch (healthy → unreachable → drain past the window → reset), and the honest result-record shape.
- **`src/queue/file-queue.ts`** — `FileJobQueue`: a directory tree (`pending/ processing/ done/ results/`), no redis/sqlite. Claim is an **atomic rename** (`pending/ → processing/`) — the rename is the mutex, so exactly one worker wins a job even across processes. Backpressure refusal, poison-job → failed-result, `unclaim` for retry.
- **`src/queue/worker.ts`** — the worker loop: claims jobs, runs the gpu-tier analyzer against the resident service (reusing `ocr.unlimited`'s `serve.json` / `ELIZA_GPU_VISION_URL` endpoint discovery via the analyzer itself), merges results into `analysis.json`. Hard per-job wall-clock timeout; requeue-on-transient; **drain-to-skip** once the outage outlasts `drainAfterMs`.
- **`src/queue/analysis-merge.ts`** — atomic read-modify-write of `analysis.json` (temp + rename), so a reader never sees a torn document while results stream in.
- **`src/analyzers/executor.ts`** — the `AnalyzerExecutor` seam extracted from the runner (`InlineExecutor` is the default; runner behaviour unchanged). **`src/queue/executor.ts`** — `QueueExecutor` routes gpu-tier analyzers through the queue and delegates cpu/above-tier ones inline; honest `skipped-missing-tool` when no worker attaches.
- **CLI**: `evidence:gpu-queue` (`worker` + `enqueue`).

**Honest degradation everywhere:** a down service produces `skipped-missing-tool` records carrying the reason — never a fabricated empty transcript. `EvidenceError`, J-annotated catches, prose headers, no `console` in lib.

## Executor wiring

The runner's per-analyzer call site now goes through `options.executor ?? INLINE_EXECUTOR`. Default runs are byte-identical to before. Passing `new QueueExecutor(queue)` offloads gpu-tier analyzers to the shared worker instead of loading a model per image; cpu-tier analyzers and above-tier ones keep their inline semantics (including the correct `skipped-tier` record).

8b:T10e4,Closes #14705. Closes #14704. Closes #14706. (Part of the cross-connector roles validation lane; #14707/#14710/#14711/#14712 remain open with follow-up notes below.)

## What this fixes

The "Discord owner = app owner" story was half-built dead code plus two privilege-escalation holes (all adversarially verified on develop before implementation):

1. **`OWNER_BIND_VERIFY` had no producer (#14705)** — both connectors have shipped `/eliza-pair` / `/eliza_pair` pairing commands since the v2.0.4 baseline, relaying to a backend service **nothing registered**: every deployment logged "started without /eliza-pair" and the flow documented in plugin-discord's CLAUDE.md could never run.
2. **Telegram fail-open world ownership (#14704)** — `service.ts:1388` had `ownerId = canonicalOwnerId ?? userId`: with no canonical owner configured, **any DM sender became OWNER of their DM world**, clearing every `minRole: OWNER` gate (SHELL, SECRETS). Same hole class #12087 Item 2 closed in core.
3. **ADMIN → OWNER escalation via identity merge (#14706)** — CONTACT link/merge (ADMIN-gated) could link an ADMIN's entity to the owner entity; the confirmed `identity_link` then resolves to OWNER everywhere, bypassing `canModifyRole`'s "ADMIN never grants OWNER".

## Implementation

- **`packages/agent/src/services/owner-binding.ts`** — `OwnerBindingService` registers `OWNER_BIND_VERIFY` (wired in `eliza-plugin.ts`, boots before connectors so the pairing commands now register). Crypto-random 6-digit codes, sha256 at rest, constant-time compare, single-use, 5-min TTL, 5-attempt cap, issuance refused when no canonical owner. On verify it writes the platform identity onto the **owner entity's metadata** — the exact shape `connectorIdentityMatches` already resolves to OWNER. Generic across connectors; zero core changes.
- **`packages/agent/src/actions/pair-owner-account.ts`** — `PAIR_OWNER_ACCOUNT` (roleGate OWNER + in-handler recheck): owner says "link my discord" in the app → gets the code + the exact `/eliza-pair` command; codes never revealed to non-owners.
- **`packages/agent/src/actions/contact.ts`** — `guardOwnerIdentityLink`: link/merge touching an owner-equivalent entity (configured owners ∪ fallback admin entity ∪ world owner) is denied unless the sender is OWNER (`OWNER_LINK_FORBIDDEN`). Also fixes the op-dispatch so `op:merge action:accept` is reachable.
- **`plugins/plugin-telegram/src/world-ownership.ts`** — ownership falls back only to the group creator, never the message sender.

- `owner-binding.test.ts` (15): replay-after-success, brute-force burn, expiry, cross-connector isolation, imposter with wrong code, malformed input, write-failure fail-closed, metadata merge.
- `pair-owner-account.test.ts` (12): imposter denied through the **real** role machinery, no code leakage, per-connector commands, ambiguous/unavailable/failure paths.
- `contact.owner-guard.test.ts` (8): ADMIN denied linking/merging to owner + fallback entity, OWNER allowed, unrelated pairs unaffected, reject needs no authority.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)8c:T13c6,## What

First-time-user (FTU) **goal-discovery** experience + **anticipation-feedback** loop, built entirely on the existing provider/evaluator patterns — no new scheduling or double-processing machinery.

- **`ftuGoal` provider** (`plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/providers/ftu-goal.ts`, position `-5`, private surfaces + owner only): once first-run is complete but no primary owner goal is known, injects a compact instruction to discover what the owner values by weaving ONE natural question into the reply. Goes silent the moment a goal is recorded.
- **`ftu_goal_discovery` evaluator** (`src/lifeops/ftu-goal/evaluator.ts`) + **state store** (`src/lifeops/ftu-goal/state.ts`): runs in the **single merged post-turn `EvaluatorService` call**, parses the goal + confidence, and its processor persists the goal to `OwnerFactStore` and flips FTU-goal state to `complete` at/above the confidence threshold. `shouldRun` is `false` once complete → **no reprocessing**.
- **`anticipation_feedback` evaluator** (`src/lifeops/anticipation/evaluator.ts`) + **marker store** (`src/lifeops/anticipation/store.ts`): when the agent's prior turn was a proactive dispatch, classifies the owner's response (accepted / ignored) against recorded dispatch markers, counts older markers as ignored, removes markers so a turn is never classified twice, and keeps durable rolling stats to tune proactivity.
- Both evaluators registered in the plugin (`src/plugin.ts`); scheduler wiring records proactive-dispatch markers (`src/lifeops/scheduled-task/scheduler.ts`).

Minimizes work: reuses the merged single-model post-turn evaluator call (no extra model calls), the runtime cache stores, `OwnerFactStore`, and the existing provider position/gating conventions.
